value_proposition: Independent, vendor-agnostic enterprise software advisory that helps organisations reduce licence and subscription costs, maintain compliance, mitigate audits and implementation risk, and negotiate more effectively with major software vendors. The company claims clients save 21% on average through licensing restructuring and contract renegotiation, although the supplied evidence does not explain the calculation methodology.
target_customers: Organisations with significant enterprise software and cloud investments
Enterprise IT, procurement, commercial, finance, applications and vendor-management leaders
Organisations facing software licence audits or intellectual-property infringement claims
Organisations negotiating new software contracts or renewals
Organisations considering ERP upgrades, replacements, cloud migrations or hybrid ERP models
Organisations moving to third-party software maintenance
Public-sector agencies, utilities, universities and multinational organisations

The website says the company does not resell or implement next-generation ERP products.

Client-side ERP implementation governance and advocacy rather than ERP implementation by Invictus Partners
Services delivered across multiple international regions

Executive, stakeholder and Board communication support
Independent quality assurance and program-risk mitigation
ERP requirements gathering, roadmap creation and market evaluation

geographic_presence: The company claims client work across Australia, Europe, the United Kingdom, the Middle East and the United States
strengths: Broad coverage across software strategy, sourcing, licensing, audits, cloud, ERP and third-party support
Stated vendor-agnostic model: the company says it neither resells nor implements next-generation ERP products, reducing an apparent source of channel conflict
Services can be purchased end-to-end or as separate engagements and customised to client circumstances
Vendor-specific practices cover major enterprise vendors and cloud platforms, including SAP, Oracle, Microsoft, IBM, AWS, Google Cloud Platform, VMware and ServiceNow
Named customer case studies provide evidence of work in ERP planning, licence optimisation, audit defence and third-party maintenance preparation
International office footprint spanning Australia, Singapore, the United States, the United Kingdom and South Africa
Website claims a leadership team with more than 225 years of combined enterprise software vendor and systems-integrator experience

Customer evidence reports measurable outcomes, including a cited 24% reduction in Microsoft Azure subscription costs and other cited licence savings around or above 20%; these remain customer testimonials rather than independently validated results
weaknesses: No public pricing, standard service packages, contract terms or typical engagement duration are disclosed
The supplied evidence describes advisory methodologies but provides little detail about proprietary technology, automation or a client-facing software platform
No integrations, APIs or developer tooling are identified
Many customer examples are anonymised, limiting verification and assessment of customer scale
The claim of being truly objective is supported by the stated no-resale/no-implementation model, but the website does not disclose all referral, alliance or compensation arrangements
The claimed average savings and cumulative client savings are not accompanied by definitions, sample sizes, time periods or independent verification
Industry coverage is implied mainly through case studies and testimonials rather than an explicit industry strategy
The collected partnerships page is unavailable and provides no evidence of formal partnerships
competitive_differentiators: Claims independence from software-vendor resale and ERP implementation revenue
Advises on options including doing nothing, upgrading, migrating, replacing or extending existing systems beyond end-of-support
Combines commercial negotiation, licensing compliance, Software Asset Management and ERP transformation advice
Personnel are presented as having worked across software vendors, systems integrators, support providers and client organisations
Can negotiate directly with vendors or advise clients behind the scenes
Offers both point-in-time licence health checks and ongoing managed licence or vendor-management services
Positions itself explicitly as a client advocate seeking to shift negotiating power away from large software vendors

Uncertainty about actual usage compared with contractual entitlements
Software compliance exposure and punitive audit outcomes

Vendor lock-in and pressure to follow vendor ERP roadmaps
Bias created by advisors that also resell or implement software
Rising cloud IaaS, PaaS and SaaS costs
Difficulty managing numerous software vendors and suppliers

technical_risks: Licence-position accuracy depends on complete and accurate usage, deployment, entitlement and contract data from the client and its vendors
Major vendors' changing product metrics, cloud models, audit practices and contract terms may make analysis difficult to maintain
The website does not disclose the architecture, security controls, data-handling practices or automation supporting managed licence services
Customised and expert-led delivery may create dependence on specialist personnel and consistent execution
ERP recommendations and implementation governance cannot by themselves ensure implementation success because Invictus Partners states it does not implement the ERP platform
No technical details are provided for ILMT-as-a-Service, SAM tooling, monitoring frequency, data collection or supported integration methods
business_risks: The model appears substantially dependent on specialist consulting labour and vendor-specific expertise
Demand may be influenced by enterprise vendor audit activity, contract cycles, ERP end-of-support events and migration programs
The company advises on products from large vendors whose licensing or contracting changes could require continual capability investment
Its confrontational marketing may appeal to dissatisfied buyers but could be unsuitable for organisations seeking a more neutral tone or collaborative vendor messaging
The evidence does not disclose revenue, profitability, ownership, funding, employee count or customer concentration
The absence of disclosed formal partnerships may limit ecosystem reach, although it may also support the independence positioning
Performance and savings claims could create elevated customer expectations without disclosed measurement standards
marketing_message: Invictus Partners uses direct, provocative language—such as “Are you getting screwed by your software vendor?” and “We swear so you don’t have to”—to position itself as an independent client advocate that helps enterprises reclaim control from major software vendors, reduce cost, realise value and remain compliant. Its mission is to create $2 billion in global enterprise software savings; the website says it is just shy of $1.2 billion, making the $2 billion figure a future goal rather than a current achievement.
messaging_gaps: No clear explanation of how the claimed 21% average client savings or nearly $1.2 billion cumulative savings are calculated or verified
No quantified audit-defence success rate, ERP project success rate or managed-service performance indicators
No clear comparison against named competitor categories beyond the general claim that some competitors sell endorsed software
No explanation of the proprietary assets, data, benchmarks or technology underpinning its methodologies
No defined service-level commitments, delivery timelines or typical project scope
No security, privacy, data-residency or compliance positioning for services that may access sensitive contracts and deployment data
No formal customer segmentation by company size, software expenditure or geographic market
